newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai feedmill chief says corn quota not enough.
newsitem.headline: Thai feedmill chief says corn quota not enough.

text.p: The Thai feedmill industry's demand for corn in the near term will exceed the 200,000-tonne zero-tariff import quota allowed by the government, Prasit Damrongchietanon, president of the Thai Feed Mill Association, told Reuters.
He said the minimum demand for imports would be around 300,000 tonnes.
But so far, most operators had not ordered any corn yet as they were waiting for the final word by the commerce ministry.
The ministry earlier allowed the imports on condition that the average prices of domestic supplies reached 4.50 baht a kg at Bangkok silos.

"The prices have reached that level. We expect to hear good news from the government after Songkran holidays," he said on Thursday. Songkran is the Thai New Year festival and the holidays start this weekend and end on April 15.
Prasit said he hoped that the government would raise the quota amount.
"But it depends on local corn price movements during the imports. If the prices steady or firm despite the imports, we hope the government will consider increasing quota," he said.
The industry is likely to import the corn from South America, especially Argentina as the price is most attractive.
"I don't think we are going to import from China. The C&F price of South American origin is cheaper than that from China by $10-15 per tonne," Prasit said.
